title: Typological Split Permutation Test and Meta-Analysis
summary: This evaluation validates the post-hoc typological split in temporal dependency overlap across 86 UD treebanks through five analyses. (1) A 10,000-iteration permutation test confirms the 1.58 SD VSO-SOV gap is highly significant (p < 0.0001 for both gap and Kruskal-Wallis H), with all pairwise Mann-Whitney tests significant after Bonferroni correction. (2) DerSimonian-Laird random-effects meta-analysis stratified by word order: VSO pooled d=+1.04 (CI [0.79,1.28], p≈0), SVO pooled d=+0.12 (p=0.077), SOV pooled d=-0.49 (p<10⁻¹³), overall d=-0.04 (p=0.53). Raw LLF meta-analysis confirms similar patterns. (3) Head-final proportion correlates strongly with residualized LLF d: Pearson r=-0.80 (p<10⁻²⁰), bootstrap 95% CI [-0.86,-0.71], partial r=-0.80 controlling for n_sentences, across all 86 treebanks. (4) VSO leave-one-out is robust: min gap=1.54, all permutation p<0.05, max influence (ga_idt) causes only 0.04 gap drop. VSO families: Afro-Asiatic(2), Indo-European(4), Tupian(1). (5) Prediction scorecard: 2/10 confirmed (DC2, DC3 disconfirmations), 5/10 failed (SC1-SC5), 3/10 inconclusive. Output: 96 examples (86 treebanks + 10 criteria), 112 aggregate metrics. Schema-validated against exp_eval_sol_out.json.
